newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam dismisses U.S. human rights report.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam dismisses U.S. human rights report.

text.p: Vietnam's communist government dismissed on Saturday the latest U.S. State Department annual report on human rights in which Hanoi's record for upholding freedoms was described as poor.
A foreign ministry spokesperson dictated a one sentence response to press queries:
"We wish to state that no nation has the right to decide and impose views on human rights against other countries," she said, reading from a prepared statement.
The State Department report, released in Washington on Thursday, criticised a number of Asian countries including Vietnam.
"The Government's (Hanoi's) human rights record continued to be poor," it said. "The Government continued to repress basic political and some religious freedoms and to commit numerous abuses."

It referred to reports that some prisons were employing the use of forced labour for commercial ventures, quoted estimates that Vietnam was holding between 70 and 1,000 political prisoners, and criticised the behaviour of members of the powerful internal security agency.
Vietnam has reacted with anger on several occasions to criticism of its human rights record from overseas.
Party officials say rights issues are being used as a pretext for subversion by forces intent on undermining confidence in Vietnam's socialist system.
